name: El Niño
description: El Niño is a natural climate pattern in which parts of the tropical Pacific Ocean become unusually warm. It changes weather around the world, causing droughts in some places and heavier rain or flooding in others.

metrics.name: Agriculture share of GDP
metrics.description: The share of agriculture in the total GDP of a country.

metrics.name: Agriculture share of Labour
metrics.description: The share of agriculture in the total labor force of a country.
metrics.example: Agriculture employs more than 70% of the national labor force

metrics.name: Cropland
metrics.description: Hectares of cropland affected by droughts or flood in an El Niño event since 1997, national and subnational data points
metrics.example: More than 35% of cultivated land in the south was completely dry, with no harvest expected until the following rainy season.

metrics.name: Pastureland
metrics.description: Hectares of pastureland affected by droughts or flood in an El Nino event since 1997, national and subnational data points
metrics.example: More than 40% of pastureland in the north was completely dry, with no grazing expected until the following rainy season.

metrics.name: Crop yield loss
metrics.description: Crop yield loss as a result of drought or flood during an El Nino event since 1997, national and subnational data points
metrics.example: Among households surveyed in 14 affected districts, 51% reported harvests more than 50% lower than in 2023. Nearly 720,000 tonnes of maize were lost, valued at about USD 349 million and equivalent to roughly 7% of agricultural GDP

metrics.name: Livestock loss
metrics.description: Livestock loss as a result of drought or flood during an El Nino event since 1997, national and subnational data points
metrics.example: In the worst-affected areas, over 30% of livestock were lost, amounting to an estimated USD 247 million in economic losses.

metrics.name: Damage to agriculture infrastructure
metrics.description: Damage to agriculture infrastructure or productive assets as a result of drought or flood during an El Nino event since 1997, national and subnational data points
metrics.example: Prolonged flooding damaged up to 80–95% of irrigated farms in some areas.

metrics.name: Change in livelihood
metrics.description: Change in livelihood or farming decision as a result of drought or flood during an El Nino event since 1997
metrics.example: Crop failure then forced more than half of the households surveyed to replant, while some were unable to do so because they lacked seeds or weather conditions remained unfavorable.Crop and income losses pushed some farming households to borrow money to purchase seed and meet basic needs, increasing debt and the risk of selling productive assets

metrics.name: Coping strategies
metrics.description: Farmers or pastoralists coping strategies to drought or flood during an El Nino event since 1997
metrics.example: 26% sold livestock to meet immediate needs, mainly food, while 25% consumed seed stocks intended for the next planting season

metrics.name: Subsequent hazards
metrics.description: Subsequent hazards that have an impact on agriculture during an El Nino event since 1997
metrics.example: Drought was compounded by fall armyworm attacks on maize and other crops reported by surveyed households, illustrating that the agricultural consequences of an El Niño season are not confined to rainfall deficits alone. Drought impacts were compounded by pest outbreaks, including rat infestations, and affected rice, corn, vegetables and other crops.

metrics.name: Food prices
metrics.description: Food price increase as a result of drought or flood during an El Nino event since 1997
metrics.example: Food prices were around 40% above the five-year average, while maize prices had more than doubled year-on-year

metrics.name: Supply and trade disruptions
metrics.description: Supply and trade disruption as a result of drought or flood during an El Nino event since 1997
metrics.example: the country contracted a record 1.35 million tonnes of rice imports

metrics.name: Hunger
metrics.description: Incident of Hunger or food insecurity during an El Nino event since 1997
metrics.example: Between April and September 2024, 2.79 million people faced IPC Phase 3 or worse acute food insecurity
